LESSON: READING 13.4.1 SHORT STORY: STYLE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does a writer make a story interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify personification and flashback in a short story
2. read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback
3. appreciate the creative use of language in short stories

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 13.4.1 SHORT STORY: STYLE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 13.4.1 SHORT STORY: STYLE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify personification and flashback in a short story

What this means
In this part you learn to identify personification and flashback in a short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify personification and flashback in a short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify personification and flashback in a short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback

What this means
In this part you learn to read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the creative use of language in short stories

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the creative use of language in short stories. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the creative use of language in short stories.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the creative use of language in short stories. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify personification and flashback in a short story)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style to a partner. (skill: read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the creative use of language in short stories)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify personification and flashback in a short story.
3. Practise this skill: read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the creative use of language in short stories.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does a writer make a story interesting?
2. Which qualities of a person can be given to animals?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify personification and flashback in a short story.
5. Be able to: read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
